author: kirubaharan181
description: Coordinates live incidents: severity, roles, comms, timeline, recovery. Use when an incident is active. Do NOT use for routine support tickets.
purpose: Provides command and coordination during an active incident: it classifies severity, assigns roles, sets escalation and communication cadence, keeps a timeline and decision log, coordinates recovery and hands over to the post-incident review. It coordinates people and decisions; it does not perform the technical fix and it never claims an incident was handled when no incident was run.
when_to_use: An incident is declared or a service is failing and impact is unclear.
Several teams must coordinate, communicate and decide quickly.
A timeline and decision log must be kept for later review.
when_not_to_use: Designing monitoring or writing the postmortem analysis: use sre-observability.
prerequisites: A way to reach the on-call people and stakeholders.
A shared place for the timeline and decision log.
No external API keys, paid services or network access are required; work uses files and tools already approved in the repository.
outputs: recovery confirmation and handover for review

decision_rules.action: Classify as highest severity and page the incident roles.

decision_rules.situation: Cause unknown after the agreed interval
decision_rules.action: Escalate to the next tier and widen the responder group.
Consider rollback first if safe and approved.
Route through emergency change approval and record it.
Assign explicitly; one person is the incident commander.
Say what is known, unknown and when the next update comes.

quality_gates: One incident commander and named role holders
Updates sent at the agreed cadence
Every decision logged with time and owner
Recovery verified by evidence before closing

examples.title: Declare and classify
examples.request: Checkout errors are rising; payments failing for some users.
examples.context: Error rate 8 percent, started 12 minutes ago after a release.
examples.behavior: Classify high severity, assign commander, communications and technical lead, and ask whether the release can be rolled back.
examples.output: Incident record with severity, roles, first update and next update time.
examples.acceptance: Roles are named and the first update is scheduled.

examples.title: Log a decision
examples.context: Rollback is tested; data impact is none.
examples.behavior: Record options, owner, decision, time and the approval route.
examples.output: Decision log entry with rollback approved by the on-call authority.
examples.acceptance: Entry has time, owner and rationale.

examples.title: Close and hand over
examples.behavior: Confirm recovery with metrics, send the final update, and open the review with timeline.
examples.output: Closure record and handover to the postmortem owner.
examples.acceptance: Recovery is shown by data, not by statement.

limitations: Coordinates; it does not diagnose without telemetry or fix without access.
Cannot confirm facts it was not told; it marks unknowns.
Does not replace the humans who hold authority for emergency changes.

troubleshooting.resolution: Name one commander and a communications lead.

troubleshooting.error: No clear owner of the affected service
troubleshooting.resolution: Escalate to the on-call manager and record the gap.
Record each source and time; verify with data.

handoffs.artifact: timeline and decision log for root cause analysis
